name: Wisconsin
source: Income tax confirmed primary (s359, read 2026-10-24): Wisconsin Department of Revenue 2026 Form 1-ES instructions (2026 tax rate schedules A, B and C, 2026 standard deduction schedules, exemptions 700 and 250; https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2026/2026-Form1-ES-Inst.pdf), 2025 Form 1 instructions (https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2025/2025-Form1-Inst.pdf), 2025 Schedule SB instructions (Social Security subtraction, 30% capital gain exclusion, 24000/48000 retirement income subtraction; https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2025/2025-ScheduleSB-Inst.pdf), Wis. Stat. 71.05(6)(b)54m (https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/71/i/05/6/b/54m), 71.06(2e) and 71.05(22)(dt) (bracket and standard deduction indexing); second sources brackets.tax and calculover.com 2026 Wisconsin brackets, EY Tax News 2025-1727 (Act 15)

filing_tables.note: Schedule A (single and head of household), B (married filing jointly) and C (married filing separately) of the 2026 Form 1-ES instructions (https://www.revenue.wi.gov/TaxForms2026/2026-Form1-ES-Inst.pdf, read 2026-10-24).

state_base.note: Wisconsin starts from federal adjusted gross income (Form 1 line 1), so 401(k) deferrals, deductible Traditional IRA deposits and HSA deposits stay deductible as on the federal return; the Schedule AD additions and Schedule I adjustments list nothing for them (2025 Form 1 instructions, read 2026-10-24).

income_brackets.note: Every threshold, rate and base of the three tables matches the 2026 tax rate schedules A, B and C in the 2026 Form 1-ES instructions (read 2026-10-24): 3.5%, 4.4%, 5.3% and 7.65%; the bases equal the cumulative tax.

standard_deduction.note: Approximation of a sliding deduction. 2026 schedules (Form 1-ES instructions, read 2026-10-24, every figure matches): single 13960 up to 20119 of Wisconsin income, less 12% of the income over 20120, none above 136453; joint 25840 up to 29039, less 19.778% of the income over 29040, none above 159690; separate 12280 up to 13779, less 19.778% over 13780, none above 75869. The schema holds one figure, so the file uses the amount at a typical income: 60000 single (9175), 100000 joint (11800, rounded; the schedule gives 11805.53) and 50000 separate (5115); lower incomes get too little and higher ones too much. The amounts and thresholds are indexed by statute (71.05(22)(dt)); the file's indexed false is kept pending an owner decision (s359).

exemptions.note: 700 for each person and dependent, 250 more for each person aged 65 or older (2026 Form 1-ES instructions, read 2026-10-24).

retirement_exclusion.note: 2025 Wisconsin Act 15: a person aged 67 or older at year end subtracts up to 24000 of retirement income from qualified plans and IRAs; on a joint return with both spouses 67 or older the cap is 48000 combined, whichever spouse received the payments (Wis. Stat. 71.05(6)(b)54m, https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/71/i/05/6/b/54m, and the 2025 Schedule SB instructions, both read 2026-10-24); no income test. The model splits the withdrawal equally between spouses, so a couple both 67 or older gets the pooled 48000; with one spouse 67 or older the cap is 24000 on half the withdrawal. Claiming it bars any credit listed under s. 71.07 (not modelled). Not modelled: the older 5000 subtraction for people 65 or older with federal AGI under 15000 (30000 married).

capital_gains_exclusion.note: Wisconsin excludes 30% of the net capital gain on assets held more than one year (60% for farm assets, not modelled): Wis. Stat. 71.05(6)(b)9 and the 2025 Schedule SB line 5 instructions (read 2026-10-24).

estate_inheritance.note: Wisconsin levies no estate tax (its pick-up estate tax ended for deaths after 2007) and no inheritance tax (state-costs.csv columns estate_tax and inheritance_tax; Tax Foundation and Kiplinger state death-tax lists). Confirmed primary on https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/statutes/72.pdf (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

social_security.note: Social Security benefits are not taxable for Wisconsin: the taxable federal amount is subtracted (2025 Schedule SB line 4 instructions, read 2026-10-24).

local_income_tax.check_at: https://www.revenue.wi.gov (local governments levy no income tax)
local_income_tax.note: Wisconsin counties and cities levy no income tax (state-costs.csv local_income_tax 'none'; Tax Foundation local income tax list).

sales_tax.check_at: Wisconsin revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://zamp.com/resources/sales-tax-on-groceries and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: assumed equal to the combined rate. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: no); research note: Food exempt from state and county taxes. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; taxed). Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Confirmed primary on the Census ACS 2024 1-year tables (https://api.censusreporter.org/1.0/data/show/latest?table_ids=B25090,B25082&geo_ids=04000US55, validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.source: WisDOT DMV fees page: automobile annual registration fee 85 (search extract, 2026-10-23)
car_taxes.note: Floor: the flat automobile registration fee. Wisconsin levies no property tax on vehicles (WalletHub 0); the local wheel taxes of some counties and cities are not included. Set by hand (s328, 2026-10-23, owner decision C4: no 0 that only means unknown); a move changes the entered car tax by the dollar difference of the two states' figures, and the importer keeps a non-zero figure.

fuel.source: Excise: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/statistics/2023/mf205.cfm (validation run 3, 2026-10-22); price: USGasGauge state-by-year table (AAA data), 2024 annual average
fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel; average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Gas excise: 0.309, frozen since 2006 (Wis. Stat. 78.015); the former 0.329 added the 0.02 petroleum inspection fee (validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 3, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, Wisconsin insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Research note: Medigap: state-standardized plans; source substitutes nearest plan (MA = Supplement 1A). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
